candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record demonstrates a malignant B-cell lymphoproliferative process with aberrant BCL2 expression, elevated Ki-67, mixed small-to-large B lymphocytes negative for CD5/CD10, widespread nodal and extranodal disease (stage IV), chylous pleural effusion, and systemic symptoms — all consistent with high-grade follicular lymphoma. Pseudolymphoma is a benign reactive condition that would not produce this constellation of findings, widespread PET-avid adenopathy, or the immunophenotypic profile described.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Pseudolymphoma is a benign reactive lymphoid hyperplasia, not a malignant lymphoma; it does not match the reference diagnosis of high-grade (3A) follicular lymphoma stage IVB

case_quality_flags: Chylothorax (triglycerides 747 mg/dL) is an unusual but well-documented manifestation of mediastinal lymphoma compressing the thoracic duct
CD10-negative follicular lymphoma is less common but recognized, particularly in higher-grade variants
Stage IVB designation supported by retroperitoneal adenopathy and unintentional weight loss as B symptom
